title: You can carry a cross…
paragraphs:
You can carry a cross…
…and still be carrying your ego.

You can lift your hands in worship—
while your heart is still bowing to yourself.

You can say “Lord, use me”—
but secretly mean, “Lord, make me seen.”

It’s where most people live.
But few are brave enough to admit it.
Because the scariest deception isn’t rebellion.
It’s religious pride wearing God’s name.

There are people serving in church every week—
singing, preaching, leading, posting—

We celebrate platforms.
We admire gifting.
We applaud visibility.

You can look anointed…
and still be addicted to approval.

You can sound powerful…
and still be empty when the crowd disappears.

You can serve God publicly…
and serve yourself privately.
“Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.” — Luke 9:23

Not your schedule.
Not your enemies.
Yourself.

Your need to be praised.
Your need to be right.
Your need to be seen.
Some scholars interpret this “taking up the cross” as more than suffering—it’s a conscious, ongoing surrender of identity, ambition, and control to God’s will.
You don’t add Jesus to your life.
You hand Him the whole thing.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.

We don’t mind serving God—
as long as it still serves us.
But what about when it doesn’t?
What about when obedience costs you visibility?
When doing the right thing gets you nothing but silence?
That’s where true service is revealed.
Because real service is not proven in the spotlight.
And here’s the truth that changes everything:
You cannot kill pride by trying harder.
You kill pride by coming to the Cross.
Because pride isn’t just a personality issue.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
But God didn’t leave us there.
“He humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death—even death on a cross.” — Philippians 2:8
He carried a cross that wasn’t His.
For people who would reject Him.
So now the invitation is not:
“Come die with Christ… and live again.”
“I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me.” — Galatians 2:20
you’re not serving to be seen.
You’re serving because you’ve seen the Cross.
This is where shame turns into redemption.
Because maybe you’re reading this and realizing—
“I’ve been serving… but it’s been about me.”
God is not exposing you to shame you.
He’s revealing you to heal you.
So what do you do now?

“Jesus, I see it now.
My pride. My motives. My need to be seen.
I lay it down.
Not just my actions—my heart.
Change me.
Make me Yours again.”
Because the same Jesus who carried the cross—
If this pierced something in your heart—
but might be fighting pride on the inside.
